reasons: **Safety first, but it's close:** Even on a bad day, crew body temperatures should stay just under the danger line, with only about a quarter of a degree to spare. Watch for signs of heat stress and call breaks early.

**We get less done to stay safe:** This plan finishes about 18% of the most important work. Two other plans (one of them using Dev only for early scaffolding) get a little more done, about 21%, but they push the crew closer to the heat limit.
**Fixed rules built in:** No one works outside from 2 to 3 pm because of lightning. Dev is new and not used to the heat yet, so he gets no very heavy jobs during the hottest parts of the day.
Peak 90th pct core temp 37.77 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.22 °C, 18% of priority-weighted work done.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.

calls.prompt:
Write 3 short plain-language bullet points (no jargon) for a crew lead explaining this schedule's trade-offs. Facts:
Peak 90th pct core temp 37.77 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.22 °C, 18% of priority-weighted work done.
No outdoor work 14:00-15:00 (lightning).
Dev (new hire) is not acclimatized: no very heavy work in high heat.
Alternatives: llm-idea:Protect the new hire and use him for early scaffold only (21% work, peak 37.85 °C); optimizer:fairness (21% work, peak 37.87 °C)
calls.response:
- **Safety first, but it's close:** Even on a bad day, crew body temperatures should stay just under the danger line, with only about a quarter of a degree to spare. Watch for signs of heat stress and call breaks early.
- **We get less done to stay safe:** This plan finishes about 18% of the most important work. Two other plans (one of them using Dev only for early scaffolding) get a little more done, about 21%, but they push the crew closer to the heat limit.
- **Fixed rules built in:** No one works outside from 2 to 3 pm because of lightning. Dev is new and not used to the heat yet, so he gets no very heavy jobs during the hottest parts of the day.
